messages:
melissa: FYI: saw a WS resume case in canary where tenant got billed twice because the old route finalized tokens after a route-swap. Looks like a tombstone/lease expiry race.

ryan: Hmm. Is this the same as the resume-id duplicate issue? Or a separate path where the old connection finishes post-failover and still invoices?

melissa: Different enough to call out. Sequence: client disconnect -> route A starts a graceful shutdown -> client reconnects -> route B accepts resume -> route B streams tokens -> route A eventually flushes buffered tokens and posts billing event.

ankit: Logs:```
[2025-01-12T13:04:01.001Z] route=eu-ws-a session=xyz resume_id=rid-77 state=disconnect start_tokens=0
[2025-01-12T13:04:01.120Z] route-pick resume_id=rid-77 chosen=eu-ws-b reason=sticky-fallback
[2025-01-12T13:04:01.128Z] eu-ws-b resume_id=rid-77 processed_tokens=48
[2025-01-12T13:04:01.620Z] eu-ws-a flush_buffer resume_id=rid-77 flush_tokens=48 billed=yes
```
So both routes bill the same 48 tokens ~500ms apart.

melissa: Important: route A had started lease_tombstone at 13:04:00.980Z (ttl 300ms) and thought it was safe to finalize once buffer drained. We need clearer ordering between tombstone finalization and route-claim wins.

kate: From console side: we only show aggregated token counts per-tenant per-minute. Ops couldn't tell which route did the billing for that minute. We need token-level rows with resume_id & route_id to diagnose. Also add a tag in the billing UI for "suspicious duplicate" that flags resume_id collisions.

billing-bot: billing-audit: detected possible duplicate billing: tenant=acme resume_id=rid-77 amount_tokens=48 candidates=[eu-ws-a,eu-ws-b]

ryan: Short-term mitigation: block final billing if a resume event for same resume_id is observed within the tombstone window (TTL). So route A would hold finalization for TTL ms after disconnect. But that delays billing.

ankit: Alternative: route A must check lease-store before finalizing: if lease-store reports 'claimed_by != this_route' then skip billing. We already have lease claims for resume acceptance, but tombstone finalization path doesn't consult it today.

melissa: Repro (local):```bash
# simulate route swap with tiny tombstone TTL
python tests/sim_resume_tombstone.py --tombstone-ttl-ms 300 --swap-delay-ms 120 --resume-id rid-77
```
Triggers duplicate bill locally ~95% of runs.

ryan: Console/alert idea: create a metric resume_tombstone_dupes and surface per-shard heatmap so we can detect canary regions earlier. Also add a runbook: if >0.5% of resumes flagged, pause routing-policy rollout.

ankit: Implementation plan: 1) Make billing finalization consult centralized lease table (read-after-write semantics on resume lease) 2) Emit billing events with resume_id and route_id 3) Add console row-level filter for resume_id in billing explorer. 4) Short-term deploy a canary feature flag that makes finalization conservative (check lease).

kate: UX: Add a small inline banner in the rollout console when the new routing policy is live: "This policy may increase resume route churn. Enable duplicate-resume-protection to avoid transient double-billing." Link to docs. Also show projected billing lag if protection enabled.

melissa: Concerns: centralized lease table is a coupling point. If it goes down we must fallback to relaxed mode and alert loudly. We'll need metrics for lease-store latency.

sre-oncall: We'll add SLOs: lease-store p95 < 5ms, error budget burn > 0.1% triggers alert. Also add a guardrail: if lease-store latency high, disable strict finalization and tag affected billing events as 'degraded-lease'.

ryan: Edge case: SSE clients that stream slowly might reopen and cause legitimate double increments if the old route flushes incremental tokens after resume. We need to define semantics: resume is authoritative and older route must not bill for tokens after resume timestamp. That implies token timestamps or sequence numbers in billing events.

ankit: We can add a "token_seq" field to streaming responses and include final_seq in billing events. Then lease-store holds the highest-seen seq per resume_id. When finalizing, route checks its flush_tokens upper seq <= lease_store.claimed_seq? If claim_seq > local_seq then skip. Simple and deterministic.

melissa: Good. Add to RFC: x-resume-seq header and token_seq metadata. Update client libs to include seq where possible. Backfill best-effort for older clients.

kate: I'll wire the billing explorer prototype with resume_id & route_id columns and a quick filter. Will put screenshots in #product-ux later today.

billing-bot: log: queued billing-backfill job for rid-77 to check duplicate window

melissa: Action items: ankit implement lease-check on finalize (feature-flagged) + add token_seq support; ryan add resume_tombstone_dupes metric + canary alert; kate update console UI and rollout banner; sre-oncall add lease-store SLO dashboard and pager rule; melissa open RFC for seq semantics and header.

ankit: Starting a small patch: will land lease consult in finalize behind FF and add unit tests for race.

ryan: I'll make a Grafana tile and alert rule.

melissa: Thanks all. We'll triage impact after telemetry lands.

(ends)
